title: Swiss catalog model version
description: models/<name>/<name>-<version>.yaml: one model at one version, and the variants it can be served as. Everything that decides what a deploy renders lives here, so a published file is immutable -- consumers pin the version and verify its digest. Cosmetic fields live in metadata.yaml beside it. A variant is a hardware and parallelism decision, not a deploy: anything site-specific (namespace, host paths, registry mirrors, route ConfigMaps) or per-deploy (replicas, scaling, scheduling, routing) is rejected here by design.

name.description: Catalog id. Unique across the catalog, and the default served-model name.

version.description: This version, semver. The file is models/<name>/<name>-<version>.yaml and a published version is immutable: consumers pin it and verify the file digest. Fix a mistake by publishing a new version, never by editing one.

servedName.description: What the engine advertises as the model name (--served-model-name), when it should differ from `name`. Renders to model.name. Defaults to `name`.

id.description: Unique within this entry. Convention: <engine>-<parallelism>-<hardware>, e.g. sglang-tp8-b300.

default.description: Preselect this variant in the UI. At most one per entry; the first variant wins if none is marked.

engine.description: The server the variant runs. mock is a stand-in server for tests, such as mock-llmd: it has no chart of its own and runs on the sglang or vllm chart through commandOverride. Every other engine's chart is its own.

chart.description: Chart name and version only. Never a repository -- the site profile maps the name to its own registry, because this file cannot know it.

version.description: One chart version, or a range of them in helm's constraint syntax. A bare version pins exactly: 0.8.0 is 0.8.0 and nothing else. A range lets a chart fix reach this model version without publishing a new one: >=0.8.0, ^0.8.0 (0.8.x from 0.8.0), >=0.8.0 <0.9.0. A deploy records the one version the range resolved to, so the deploy itself stays pinned. Prereleases match only a range that names one.

image.description: Canonical upstream engine image. The site profile rewrites the repository to its mirror; the tag is carried through as-is.

requires.description: What this variant needs to schedule at all. Preflight checks these against real nodes; the compose step renders `gpus` into model.gpus, so that key is not settable in `values`.

gpus.description: GPUs per pod. For a multi-node variant this is per pod, not per group -- total is gpus x nodes. 0 is CPU only: the pod requests no accelerator, so vendor, gpuProduct, minGpuMemoryGiB and rdma have nothing to describe.

nodes.description: Pods per group. 1, or absent, for single-node. Must equal lws.size when lws is enabled.

topology.description: How a replica runs. single-node: one pod. lws: a LeaderWorkerSet group across nodes, which needs values.lws.enabled: true. pd: prefill and decode disaggregated, which needs values.pd.enabled: true.

gpuProduct.description: Acceptable cards for the declared vendor. Any one matches. Absent means any card of that vendor. Each is the card's canonical name, not a cluster's label value: the nvidia.com/gpu.product value for nvidia (NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3), <Vendor>-<model> for others (Ascend-910B3). The labels that carry a card differ by vendor install, so swiss maps a name to them.

rdma.description: Needs an RDMA device from the shared-device plugin. Implied by topology lws, but stated where it matters.

vendor.description: Accelerator brand this variant is built for. Decides the extended resource the pod requests and the node label its product is published under -- nvidia.com/gpu and nvidia.com/gpu.product, huawei.com/Ascend910 and its own label, and so on. Singular on purpose: a CANN build of an engine is a different image with different flags than a CUDA build, so a model that runs on both publishes two variants rather than one variant claiming both.

values.description: Chart values this variant sets. Any object
